Build each stratum's design matrix and default contrasts from a sample sheet, with mzLib

diff_design.Rd

Turn a sample sheet and a model (factors with reference levels, covariates with units, batch, interactions, strata) into mzLib's design per stratum: the design matrix, its rank and aliased terms, the default contrasts with their estimability, and the design and contrast tables stats fit reads.

mzLib's AnalysisDesign.ByStratum splits the samples by stratum, and in each stratum builds one additive model: an intercept, each factor treatment-coded against its reference level, batch, each covariate as (value - centre) / scale, and any interactions. The matrix equals R's model.matrix() for the same formula. It then lists DefaultContrasts - each level against its reference, every pair when there is no reference, each covariate's slope - and judges whether each can be estimated at all from these samples.

Usage

diff_design(samples, factors = NULL, covariates = NULL, interactions = NULL,
  strata = NULL, batch = NULL, out = NULL, timeout = 60)

Arguments

samples

The sample sheet: a TSV with a header row and one row per biological sample. First column the sample id; the other columns are available by header. A column the model does not name is ignored (unused_columns).

factors

Condition factors, in column order: a list of factor_spec, or a character vector of column names (no reference: every pair of levels is compared), or a mix in a list.

covariates

Numeric covariates, in column order: a list of covariate_spec, each with its stored unit.

interactions

Two-factor interactions, as a list of pairs of factor names, e.g. list(c("condition", "sex")).

strata

Columns whose values split the samples into strata, each designed on its own (a character vector).

batch

The column holding each sample's batch, fitted as a fixed block. NULL: no batch.

out

A directory to write design_<i>.tsv (for stats_fit's design) and contrasts_<i>.tsv (for its contrasts) into, per stratum. NULL: nothing is written.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL to wait indefinitely.

Value

An mzlibr_diff_design:

- records, a data.frame with one row per (stratum, default contrast), strata in order: stratum, the stratum key; contrast_id, c1, c2, ... numbered within the stratum; label, factor=level vs factor=reference, or a slope's column; numerator and denominator, factor=level (NA for a slope); covariate, covariate_unit (the unit a slope is per, e.g. decade) and covariate_scale (e.g. years/10, centred at 50 years), NA when not a slope; estimability, "estimable", "not_estimable:confounded" or "not_estimable:rank_deficient"; and two list columns, weights (contrast weight per design column, unitless), one per entry of the stratum's column_names, and fitted_weights (contrast weight per fitted column, unitless), one per entry of its fitted_column_names - the contrasts file's row - and NULL when the contrast is not estimable. - strata, a list of mzlibr_design_stratum, named by stratum key ("all" for one stratum, else the stratum columns sorted by name as name=value joined by ;), each with: sample_count samples; sample_ids, the matrix rows, ordinal by sample id; column_names, mzLib's columns (intercept, factor=level per non-reference level, batch=level, name (per unit) for a covariate, a=level:b=level for an interaction); fitted_column_names, the columns a fit takes (the design file's coefficient columns); rank (columns); aliased_terms, terms that share a direction with another; warnings; not_run, a data.frame of the contrasts this stratum cannot run (label, reason); covariate_centres (the covariate's stored unit), the centre subtracted from each covariate; matrix and fitted_matrix, R matrices with the sample ids as row names, in coding (0/1 indicators; covariate columns in scaled units), equal to R's model.matrix(); and design_file and contrasts_file, the files written for this stratum, NA without out (and contrasts_file NA when nothing here is estimable). - samples_file, as an absolute path; sample_count samples read, across every stratum; factors, covariates and interactions as given (a covariate field NA was not given, so mzLib's default applied); stratum_columns; batch_column (NA when batch is not in the model); unused_columns; stratum_count strata; estimability_counts, default contrasts (contrasts) per verdict across strata; written, directory and file_count (files), or NULL without out; row_count rows; column_names. - caveats: how the matrix is coded and what the contrast ids mean, plus counts of contrasts that cannot be estimated or run.

When the samples cannot answer

A comparison the samples cannot separate - a condition run in only one batch - is "not_estimable:confounded", and one that needs a column no sample informs (an empty interaction cell) is "not_estimable:rank_deficient". mzLib says so instead of returning a number. The design file still holds a design that can be fitted: fitted_column_names leaves out the later of two aliased columns. Contrast ids are numbered within each stratum, so match strata by label.

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

samples

path; required. The sample sheet: a TSV with a header row and one row per biological sample. The first column is the sample id (unique, any header). Every other column is available to the model by its header; a column the model does not name is ignored and listed in unused_columns. Cells are trimmed. A factor, stratum or batch cell is used as text, exactly as written. A covariate cell is a number in the covariate's stored unit; a blank, NA or NaN covariate cell is no value, and mzLib refuses that sample by name.

wire --stdin

string[]; required; range one model term per line; fields tab-separated. The model, one term per line, its fields separated by tabs; an empty optional field is not given, so mzLib's default applies. factor NAME, optionally then REFERENCE: a condition factor treatment-coded against REFERENCE (FactorSpec); with no REFERENCE every pair of its levels is compared and mzLib warns. covariate NAME UNIT, optionally then SCALE, SCALED_UNIT and CENTRE: a numeric column entered as (value - CENTRE) / SCALE (CovariateSpec). UNIT is the stored unit (years); SCALE is stored units per scaled unit (10), default 1; SCALED_UNIT names the unit a slope is per (decade), default SCALE stored units; CENTRE is in the stored unit, default the stratum's mean. interaction FIRST SECOND: the two-factor interaction of two named factors. stratum NAME: a column whose value splits the samples into strata, each designed on its own. batch NAME: the column holding each sample's batch, fitted as a fixed block whenever it is named (mzLib's DesignSpec.FitBatch default; the bridge never sets it). Factors and covariates enter in the order given. A column has one role, and is named once. Not an argument here: the model is the factors, covariates, interactions, strata and batch arguments, sent one stdin line per term.

out

path; default absent. A directory (created if absent) to write the pivot files into: for stratum i in the order of strata, design_i.tsv and, when any contrast is estimable there, contrasts_i.tsv. Files are numbered, not named by stratum key, because a key can hold any character a sheet cell can; each strata entry names its files. Files of the same name are overwritten. Absent, nothing is written.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

samples_file

string; never NA. Absolute path of the sample sheet.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Samples read from the sheet, across every stratum.

factors

object[]; never NA. The factors given, in order: name and reference_level (null when none was given, so every pair of levels is compared).

covariates

object[]; never NA. The covariates given, in order: name, unit, and scale, scaled_unit and centre as given (each null when not given, so mzLib's default applied).

interactions

object[]; never NA. The interactions given, in order, each as first and second.

stratum_columns

string[]; never NA. The stratum columns given; empty for one stratum.

batch_column

string; NA when no batch line: batch is not in the model. The batch column given.

unused_columns

string[]; never NA. Sheet columns after the sample id that the model does not name, in sheet order.

stratum_count

int; in strata; never NA. Designs built: one per distinct stratum key, or 1.

strata

object[]; never NA. One object per stratum, in mzLib's order (ordinal by stratum key); fields under result.tables.strata.

estimability_counts

map<string,int>; in contrasts; never NA. Default contrasts per verdict across strata: estimable, not_estimable:confounded, not_estimable:rank_deficient.

written

object; NA when no --out: nothing was written. directory (absolute) and file_count, the design and contrast files written.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Default contrasts across strata: the table's row count.

column_names

string[]; never NA. The table's columns, in order.

records (wire columns)

table; never NA. One row per (stratum, default contrast): strata in order, each stratum's contrasts in mzLib's order.

caveats

string[]; never NA. Five static caveats, plus one when any contrast is not estimable (with counts) and one when any stratum cannot run a contrast the model asks for.

Columns of records

stratum

string; never NA. The stratum key (AnalysisDesign.StratumKey): the stratum columns sorted by name, each name=value, joined by ';', with %, ; and = in a value escaped as %25, %3B and %3D; all when there is no stratum column.

contrast_id

string; never NA. c1, c2, ... in mzLib's default order, numbered within the stratum. The name a contrasts file gives the contrast.

label

string; never NA. Readable: factor=level vs factor=reference for a level, the covariate's column name for a slope (age (per decade)).

numerator

string; NA when a slope. The numerator level as factor=level.

denominator

string; NA when a slope. The reference (or earlier) level as factor=level.

covariate

string; NA when not a slope. For a slope, the covariate.

covariate_unit

string; NA when not a slope. For a slope, the unit the effect is per: SCALED_UNIT, or SCALE stored units (10 years), or the stored unit at scale 1.

covariate_scale

string; NA when not a slope. For a slope, mzLib's statement of how the stored covariate became that unit, e.g. years/10, centred at 50 years.

estimability

string; never NA. mzLib's verdict: estimable | not_estimable:confounded (the direction it needs is shared by two or more terms, e.g. a condition only ever in one batch) | not_estimable:rank_deficient (it needs a column no sample informs, e.g. an empty interaction cell). Judged on the columns divided by their lengths, so the same in any unit.

weights

float[]; in contrast weight per design column (unitless); never NA. One weight per entry of the stratum's column_names: the contrast is the weighted sum of the coefficients.

fitted_weights

float[]; in contrast weight per fitted column (unitless); NA when not estimable: no fit gives it an estimate. AnalysisDesign.FittedWeights: the weights on the stratum's fitted_column_names, the row the contrasts file writes. A fit of the fitted matrix gives with them the estimate and standard error every least-squares fit of the full matrix gives.

Fields of strata

a list of mzlibr_design_stratum, named by stratum key.

stratum

string; never NA. The stratum key, as the table's stratum column.

sample_count

int; in samples; never NA. Samples in the stratum.

sample_ids

string[]; never NA. The rows of matrix and of the design file, ordinal by sample id.

column_names

string[]; never NA. mzLib's columns: intercept; factor=level for each non-reference level; batch=level; name (per unit) for a covariate; a=level:b=level for an interaction.

fitted_column_names

string[]; never NA. AnalysisDesign.FittedColumns by name: every column at full rank, else each column kept unless it is redundant with those kept before it. The design file's coefficient columns.

rank

int; in columns; never NA. The numerical rank, by LinearModel's own full-rank test: the number of fitted columns.

aliased_terms

string[]; never NA. Terms (factor names, batch, covariate names, intercept) that share a direction with another term and so cannot be separated from it; empty at full rank.

warnings

string[]; never NA. What mzLib left out of the model or changed from the specification here, in plain words: a factor with one level, a reference level with no sample, one batch, no reference declared.

not_run

object[]; never NA. Contrasts the model asks for that this stratum cannot run, each with label and reason (not_in_stratum).

covariate_centres

map<string,float>; in the covariate's stored unit; never NA. The centre subtracted from each covariate here: the one given, else the stratum's mean.

matrix

float[][]; in coding (0/1 indicators; covariate columns in scaled units); never NA. AnalysisDesign.Matrix, one row per sample_ids entry and one value per column_names entry. Equals R's stats::model.matrix for the same formula and level order.

fitted_matrix

float[][]; in coding (0/1 indicators; covariate columns in scaled units); never NA. AnalysisDesign.FittedMatrix: matrix with only the fitted columns. It has full column rank, so LinearModel.Fit takes it; it is the design file's body.

design_file

string; NA when no --out. Absolute path of design_i.tsv: header sample then fitted_column_names, then one row per sample, the fitted matrix in round-trip decimal. Exactly what stats fit --design reads.

contrasts_file

string; NA when no --out, or no contrast is estimable in this stratum. Absolute path of contrasts_i.tsv: header contrast then fitted_column_names (the design file's coefficient columns, same order), then one row per estimable contrast: contrast_id and fitted_weights. Each row is the ContrastWeights(name, weights) mzLib's EmpiricalBayes.ModerateContrasts takes for a fit of the design file: exactly what stats fit --contrasts reads, beside --design design_i.tsv (pyMzLib 0.6.0).

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error.

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

--samples missing, blank or not found; --out given without a directory; the sheet empty, header-only, with an empty or repeated column name, an empty or repeated sample id (repeats across strata included), or a row whose field count differs from its header; a covariate cell that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

a stdin line that is not factor, covariate, interaction, stratum or batch, or has the wrong number of fields; an empty name or unit; a SCALE or CENTRE that is not a finite number; a column named twice or in two roles; a second batch line; an interaction given twice; a named column the sheet does not have

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

mzLib refuses the input (its ArgumentException, reclassified): a sample with no value for a factor or covariate, a non-positive scale, batch on some samples only, an interaction naming a factor that is not in the model

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

never expected

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Each stratum's matrix is mzLib's AnalysisDesign: an intercept; each factor treatment-coded against its reference level, its other levels in ordinal order; batch against its first level; each covariate as (value - centre) / scale; then any interactions. It equals R's stats::model.matrix for the same formula and level order.

  • Only mzLib's default contrasts are listed (AnalysisDesign.DefaultContrasts): each level against its factor's reference, every pair of levels when a factor has no reference, and each covariate's slope. With an interaction in the model, a factor's contrast is its effect at the reference level of the other factor.

  • Contrast ids (c1, c2, ...) are numbered within each stratum, so one id can name different comparisons in two strata. Match contrasts across strata by label.

  • A design file holds only the fitted columns (fitted_column_names): mzLib leaves out a column that is redundant with earlier ones, because LinearModel.Fit refuses a design without full column rank. A contrast that is not estimable has no fitted weights and is not in the contrasts file.

  • Strata are never columns: each stratum gets its own design and nothing is shared between them. The individual a sample came from is never a fixed column either; it is for a mixed model's random intercept.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.diff.design

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::diff::design_with with DesignOptions

  • R (mzLibR): diff_design

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • Only DefaultContrasts is exposed. mzLib's AnalysisDesign.Between (any two levels) and Custom (weights by column name) have no wire form yet; with no reference declared, DefaultContrasts already gives every pair.

  • AnalysisSample.FromExperimentalDesign is not reachable: mzLib has no reader from MetaMorpheus's ExperimentalDesign.tsv to an IExperimentalDesign (MetaMorpheus's EngineLayer.ExperimentalDesign has one), so this verb starts from a sample sheet.

References

  • doi:10.2307/2346786: the model-formula notation (main effects and a:b interactions) that R's stats::model.matrix implements and mzLib's design matrix equals (Wilkinson and Rogers, Appl Stat 22:392, 1973)

See also

stats_fit, which reads the files out writes; diff_observations

Examples


# The MALAT1 dilution series stats_fit() analyses, described by each run's load rather than by a
# hand-made 0/1 design:
samples <- system.file("extdata", "diff", "malat_dilution_samples.tsv", package = "mzLibR")
design <- diff_design(samples, factors = list(factor_spec("malat_load", "500ng")),
  out = file.path(tempdir(), "malat_design"))
design
#> <mzlibr_diff_design> 27 samples in 1 stratum(s), 2 default contrast(s)
#>   estimable 2, not_estimable:confounded 0, not_estimable:rank_deficient 0
#>   all: 27 samples, columns intercept, malat_load=125ng, malat_load=250ng
stratum <- design$strata[["all"]]
stratum$fitted_column_names
#> [1] "intercept"        "malat_load=125ng" "malat_load=250ng"
design$records[, c("contrast_id", "label", "estimability")]
#>   contrast_id                                label estimability
#> 1          c1 malat_load=125ng vs malat_load=500ng    estimable
#> 2          c2 malat_load=250ng vs malat_load=500ng    estimable
design$records$fitted_weights
#> [[1]]
#> [1] 0 1 0
#> 
#> [[2]]
#> [1] 0 0 1
#>
